note: Wed 11 Nov 2026 07:02 SGT run. Tuesday Nov 10 US close: a hot October CPI print (core +0.3% vs +0.2% consensus) pushed December Fed hike odds to 100% (from 84%), hitting gold/silver/miners and crypto hard while the S&P eased only 0.38% (VIX little-changed at 19.46) -- but breadth deteriorated sharply underneath: NYSE decliners led advancers roughly 2.3-2.5:1 (secondary-sourced, two close but non-identical figures), a sharp reversal from Monday's ~81% advancing, and both S&P and Nasdaq new-highs-minus-lows worsened. CNN's own Fear & Greed page remains geo-blocked (HTTP 451); the headline value (33, Fear) is corroborated by two independent mirrors (worldmonitor.app, feargreedmeter.com) ticking up marginally from 31/32 the prior day, but the 7-component numeric breakdown could not be refreshed for a second straight run and is carried forward -- treat components as unavailable, not merely stale. Crypto Fear & Greed rose to 32 (Fear) from 29, narrowing but not closing the divergence versus equity sentiment. Breadth sourcing is unusually messy this run: %S&P500>200DMA readings from different secondary aggregators range from 37% to 67% and do not reconcile, and the McClellan Oscillator has two directly conflicting readings (+117 vs -185.1) from different vendor families -- both are flagged as unresolved rather than picking one. Flows: no newer Lipper/EPFR/BofA weekly cut exists yet (still week ending Nov 4); supplementary BofA Flow Show figures for that same week were added (global equity funds +$89.2B, a 20-week high). Next cut expected Thu/Fri Nov 12-13, covering the week that includes today's CPI shock.

breadth.note: The CPI-driven pullback was far more damaging to breadth than to the headline index: decliners swamped advancers ~2.3-2.5:1 and both the S&P and (especially) Nasdaq new-highs/lows deteriorated sharply, even though the S&P itself fell only 0.38%. That gap -- a calm index, a rough breadth tape -- is itself the signal this run: participation is narrowing under the hawkish-Fed repricing even where the headline hasn't shown it yet. %>200DMA and the McClellan Oscillator both have unreconciled, conflicting secondary readings and should be treated as directional color only until a primary source is checked.
